name: LM4950TSX_NOPB
title: LM4950: 3.1 W per channel stereo or 7.5 W bridged audio power amplifier, 9.6 V to 16 V
summary: The LM4950 holds two audio power amplifiers for a 9.6 V to 16 V supply, aimed at flat-panel monitors and TVs. From 12 V it gives 3.1 W per channel into 4 Ω single-ended at 1% THD+N, or 7.5 W into an 8 Ω bridged load at 10% THD+N. Gain is set by external resistors and the amplifiers are stable at unity gain; no bootstrap or snubber parts are needed. It has an active-low shutdown (40 µA typical), click-and-pop suppression, short-circuit protection and thermal shutdown, in a 9-lead DDPAK or TO-220.

notes: TS is the DDPAK in tubes of 45, TSX the same part on reels of 500. The TO-220 (NEC0009A) has the same pinout and thermal figures.

circuits.title: Typical bridge-tied-load (BTL) application
circuits.description: One audio input drives an 8 Ω speaker bridged across both outputs. Amplifier A is an inverting stage with gain RFA/RINA; amplifier B takes A's output through RINB and inverts it again with RFB = RINB, so the two outputs swing in opposite phase and the bridge gain is 2(RFA/RINA). CINA blocks DC from the source; CBYPASS filters the half-supply bias and sets the start-up ramp; CS bypasses the supply at pin 6.
notes: The audio source's return goes to ground.

circuits.title: Typical stereo single-ended (SE) application
circuits.description: Two independent inverting channels, each with gain RF/RIN = 1, drive 4 Ω speakers to ground. The outputs sit at half supply, so each speaker is fed through a 470 µF coupling capacitor that blocks the DC. CIN on each input blocks DC from the source; CBYPASS filters the internal bias; CS bypasses the supply.

circuits.title: BTL drive of a piezo-electric transducer (capacitance ≤ 200 nF)
circuits.description: The bridged circuit with the speaker replaced by a piezo transducer of up to 200 nF. A 33 pF capacitor across each 20 kΩ feedback resistor keeps the amplifiers stable into the capacitive load. Dissipation in the part stays low, typically under 250 mW with a 200 nF transducer at VDD = 12 V.
notes: The audio source's return goes to ground.

operation.text: Amplifier A sets the gain with RINA and RFA. Its output also feeds amplifier B through a 20 kΩ resistor, and B's 20 kΩ feedback makes B a unity inverter, so the two outputs carry equal signals of opposite phase. A load between them sees twice the swing of a single-ended stage, ideally four times the power for the same supply, provided the outputs neither clip nor current-limit. Both outputs rest at half supply, so the bridged load carries no DC and needs no output capacitor; a single-ended load fed directly would carry the half-supply DC, raising dissipation and risking speaker damage.

TJMAX is 150 °C. In the KTW (DDPAK) package θJA is 20 °C/W with the tab soldered to at least 16 in² of copper, which may be split between the top and bottom of a two-layer board, the layers joined under the tab by a 5 × 5 via array. The NEC (TO-220) package needs an external heatsink below 20 °C/W. When the worst-case dissipation exceeds what the package allows, lower the supply, raise the load impedance, lower the ambient or add heatsinking; extra copper on the ground, supply and output pins helps. Speakers rated 4 Ω (SE) or 8 Ω (BTL) must not dip below 3 Ω or 6 Ω. Dissipation falls with output power or duty cycle, which allows higher ambients.
No pin may exceed its absolute maximum voltage to ground.

A local 1.0 µF tantalum capacitor goes from VDD to ground, with short leads, even when a regulator already has 10 µF and 0.1 µF on its output. A ceramic in its place can make the amplifier oscillate. A 10 µF CBYPASS on the BYPASS pin steadies the internal bias and improves PSRR; larger values improve PSRR further but lengthen turn-on and can worsen click and pop.

Shutdown is active low and turns off the bias circuitry; supply current drops to 40 µA typical when SHUTDOWN is driven as near GND as possible, and a higher low level can raise it. With a switch: a 100 kΩ pull-up from SHUTDOWN to VDD and a second 100 kΩ from SHUTDOWN to GND in parallel with an SPST switch; the divider keeps the pin at no more than VDD/2, the switch open runs the amplifier and closed shuts it down, and the pin never floats. From a microcontroller, drive the pin from a digital output whose high level stays at or below VDD/2.
CIN is chosen from the lowest frequency to be amplified and from turn-on transient behaviour; keeping it no larger than the bandwidth needs reduces clicks and pops.

At turn-on, from power-up or leaving shutdown, an internal current source charges CBYPASS toward VDD/2. During the ramp the internal amplifiers run as unity-gain buffers disconnected from the output pins; when BYPASS reaches VDD/2 and settles they reconnect and the part is fully on. The BYPASS current is fixed, so CBYPASS sets turn-on time (120 ms at 1.0 and 2.2 µF, 200 ms at 4.7 µF, 440 ms at 10 µF). A slower ramp gives a smaller pop. CBYPASS = 10 µF with CIN between 0.1 µF and 0.39 µF gives click-free and pop-free shutdown. Every capacitor must be discharged before turn-on, so quickly cycling VDD can cause pops. The time constant of CIN with Ri + Rf should be shorter than the turn-on time set by CBYPASS.

Capacitive piezo transducers up to 200 nF can be driven, with 33 pF across each 20 kΩ feedback resistor for stability. Sound level then depends on the transducer's response and efficiency; dissipation is typically below 250 mW with 200 nF at 12 V.

For 4 W into 8 Ω BTL from 0.3 Vrms with 20 kΩ input impedance and 50 Hz to 20 kHz within ±0.25 dB: the output-power curve gives a minimum supply of 10.2 V, so 12 V leaves headroom; minimum gain is 18.9, take AV-BTL = 19; RF = 190 kΩ, use 191 kΩ, for 4 W nominal. Response must extend to one fifth of 50 Hz and five times 20 kHz (0.17 dB droop at each): fL = 10 Hz gives Ci = 0.795 µF, use 0.82 µF. With AVD = 7 and fH = 100 kHz the closed-loop gain-bandwidth product is 700 kHz, below the part's 3.5 MHz GBWP.

The DDPAK reference boards are two-layer: one in SE form for speakers of 4 Ω minimum, one in BTL form for an 8 Ω minimum speaker, both run from an external 12 V supply. The 12 V supply and ground connect to the VDD and GND pads; the speaker connects between the OUTA and OUTB outputs.
ESD protection on chip is limited; store and handle the part with its leads shorted or in conductive foam.
